add.title: La doppia sofferenza delle trans in carcere | la Repubblica Inchieste
add.summary: la Repubblica inchiesta (28 Aug 2013), 'La doppia sofferenza delle trans in carcere': documents that trans women in Italian prisons live with the 'double suffering' of being held in men's sections because official documents (carta d'identità) still list them as male; female hormones cannot be prescribed to detainees whose ID says male, decisions bounce between prison directors and doctors with no national guideline, and some facilities allow hormone treatment only if the detainee pays for it. The case of 'Smeralda' illustrates that placement follows legal/registered sex rather than gender identity.

add.title: Italy 'to open first prison for transgender inmates' | BBC News
add.summary: BBC News (Jan 2010): Italy announced it would open one of the world's first prisons dedicated to transgender inmates at Pozzale, near Florence (Tuscany), converting an almost empty medium-security prison to house trans inmates mainly convicted of drug-related offences and prostitution; Italian gay-rights groups welcomed the move. The plan was never realized (per 2013 reporting), so no dedicated trans facility exists and trans prisoners continue to be placed in ordinary facilities.
